Here’s how to do it in Outlook on Windows/Mac (desktop app). If you’re on Outlook on the web, I’ll note differences at the end.

1) Open the event
1. In Outlook, go to **Calendar**.
2. Navigate to **December 11, 2025**.
3. Find **“Panel Discussion”** (09:00–11:00).
4. **Double‑click** the event to open it (make sure it opens in its own window, not just a preview).

2) Change the date and time
5. In the event window, find the **Start time** and **End time** fields.
6. Change:
   - **Start date** from **12/11/2025** → **12/15/2025**
   - **End date** from **12/11/2025** → **12/15/2025**
7. Make sure the **start time** is **9:00 AM** and the **end time** is **11:00 AM**.
8. Confirm the **Time zone** (often shown as a link or dropdown near the times) is set to **Central Time (US & Canada)** or matches your DFW time zone.
9. Do **not** change the attendees or location, so everything else stays the same.

3) Send the update to everyone
10. Once the date/time look right, click **Send Update** (or **Send** in newer Outlook versions) in the top-left of the event window.
    - If Outlook asks whether to send updates to everyone or only to added/changed attendees, choose **Send updates to all attendees**.

That will move “Panel Discussion” to **Monday, 12/15/2025, 09:00–11:00 Central** and send the updated invite to everyone.

If you’re using **Outlook on the web** instead:
1. Go to **Outlook → Calendar** in your browser.
2. Click the event on **Dec 11, 2025**, then click **Edit** (the pencil icon) → **Edit event**.
3. Change the **date** fields to **Dec 15, 2025** and **time** to **9:00 AM–11:00 AM**.
4. Click **Send** at the top to send the update to all attendees.
